items.title: Learning & Stack Transitions
items.description: Across 8 years the primary stack has shifted several times: starting in C# and Salesforce, moving into Node.js / TypeScript and NestJS, and more recently extending to Python and Flutter. New technology is always validated by something shippable — Bound was built in Flutter and released on both iOS and Android, and the RAG framework uses no off-the-shelf package, with retrieval and evaluation implemented directly.

items.title: Team Leadership & Development Standards
items.description: Leading an 11-person cross-functional team meant turning delivery quality from individual capability into process: architecture decisions settled before work began, implementation quality held by code review, release risk controlled by a checklist and process rules, troubleshooting steps documented. Explicit rules and acceptance criteria are also what later made adopting AI possible.

items.title: Product Thinking
items.description: Most of these products were scoped by me: Bound ran from product strategy and UI design through full-stack implementation, and Coffee Chat was product, design, and both ends built alone. Feature trade-offs answer to business outcomes — subscription billing gained auto-renewal and failed-payment retries, and AI features were designed around whether they could join a paid plan rather than built first and justified later.

items.title: Performance & Cost Awareness
items.description: Performance and cloud cost belong in the design, not in a fix after launch. Indexes are designed around actual query shapes and verified against slow-query logs; caching runs in two tiers, in-process memory and Redis. Reworking the resource architecture and caching cut monthly cloud spend by 60% and brought first paint from 10s to 1.4s.

items.title: AI Applications & AI-Assisted Development
items.description: AI is both product and tooling. On the product side, four Claude subscription features shipped alongside a self-built RAG and evaluation framework with quality metrics running in CI. On the development side, standards are written as agent-readable rule files with automated verification loops so the agent judges whether it has met them, while the architecture prevents AI from blocking payments, matching, or other critical paths.

items.title: End-to-End Delivery
items.description: A full product line delivered alone: schema design, APIs, frontend, and deployment all owned directly, with no handoff between roles. Node.js / NestJS on the backend, React / Next.js on the frontend, TypeScript shared across both; frontend performance sits in the same scope.
